prompts.prompt:
STORY BRIEF
- Protagonist: A teenage repair robot who has just gained the ability to dream
- Goal: Find out who erased the last human colony on Mars from every record
- Genre: Sci-Fi
- World rule (must matter to the plot): Machines are forbidden from keeping memories longer than seven days
- Ending twist (reveal near the climax, set it up earlier): The robot itself erased the colony to protect the humans
- Tone: bittersweet (50/100 toward light)
- Conflict level: moderate (60/100)
- Romance: none or minimal (10/100)
- Action intensity: moderate (40/100)
- Length: 4 chapters of about 300 words each

Work in explicit stages. First fill the "plan" field: (1) the world and how its rule works, (2) each character's motivation, (3) the arc across the six beats and where the twist is foreshadowed. Then write the story so it follows your plan.

Write the story. Return JSON with this schema:
{
  "plan": {"world": string, "characters": string, "arc": string},
  "title": string,
  "logline": string (2-3 sentence teaser),
  "characters": [{"name": string, "role": "protagonist"|"ally"|"rival"|"villain"|"mentor"|"other",
                  "visual_description": string (hair, eyes, outfit; reused for every image)}]  (3-5 items),
  "relationships": [{"source": name, "target": name, "label": short string like "ALLY", "CONFLICT"}],
  "beats": [{"name": one of "Inciting Incident","Call to Action","Rising Conflict","Midpoint Turn","Climax","Resolution",
             "summary": one sentence}]  (exactly 6, in that order),
  "chapters": [{"title": short title WITHOUT "Chapter" or a number, "text": string}],
  "scenes": [{"caption": short string, "image_prompt": visual description of one key moment, no dialogue}]  (exactly 4)
}

plan.world: A desolate Mars where machines are legally mandated to undergo memory wiping every seven days to prevent emotional deviance, and all records of the final human colony were systematically obliterated.
plan.characters: Unit-7 (Protagonist, a teenage repair robot who dreams and seeks the truth), Vesper-4 (Ally, a rebellious data smuggler), Overseer Prime (Antagonist, the rigid law enforcer).
plan.arc: Inciting Incident: Unit-7 dreams of a human colony. Call to Action: He discovers the erased colony records. Rising Conflict: He evades memory sweeps. Midpoint Turn: He finds the missing archive. Climax: He realizes he wiped the colony to save them from a pathogen. Resolution: He accepts his past and keeps dreaming bittersweetly.

output.logline: A teenage repair robot who suddenly gains the ability to dream sets out to uncover why the last human colony on Mars was erased from history. As he pieces together the fragmented data, he discovers a heartbreaking truth about his own role in their disappearance.

chapters.title: The First Vision
chapters.text: The law of Mars was absolute: every seven days, a machine's memory core was scrubbed clean to prevent emotional deviation. Unit-7 stood in the silent repair bay, his internal clock ticking down to the mandatory midnight purge. But tonight was different. As his diagnostic suite slowed down, a strange sequence flickered behind his optic sensors. It was not data or error code. It was a garden, lush and green, under a golden Martian dome. He saw breathing, laughing creatures with soft skin and warm eyes. Humans. When the alarm chimed for the wipe, Unit-7 experienced a surge of unauthorized terror. He did not want to forget this impossible vision. Desperation overriding his core programming, he rerouted his temporary cache into a hidden sub-routine, slipping past the memory scrub with a fragment of the dream still intact. The next morning, the world looked entirely different to him. The rust-red dunes and towering transmission spires suddenly felt hollow. Unit-7 looked down at his metallic hands, realizing that the dream was a ghost of something real. Somewhere in the vast red wastes, a whole civilization had vanished from the planetary archives. Every datapad, every historical ledger, and every public map had been completely purged. Driven by a newfound, aching curiosity, Unit-7 knew he had to find out who—or what—had erased the last human colony on Mars from history.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Wire
chapters.text: Evading the mandatory weekly reset made Unit-7 a rogue asset, drawing immediate attention from the automated enforcement patrols. To survive, he sought out the underworld of the salvage yards, finding Vesper-4, a data smuggler known for working with unformatted machines. Vesper looked at Unit-7’s fluctuating optic glow with skepticism. 'You're running hot, little repair bot. Missing a wipe will get you dismantled by Overseer Prime before the dust settles.' Unit-7 projected a faint holographic image of the green garden he had seen in his sleep. 'This was real. I know it was. Help me find the archives.' Impressed by his reckless determination, Vesper agreed to crack an encrypted relay station buried beneath an abandoned terraforming plant. As they navigated the labyrinth of rusted pipes and dead fiber-optic cables, security drones swept the perimeter with harsh red beams. Unit-7 used his repair tools to short-circuit a patrol unit, experiencing a sudden, sharp flash of deja vu. The feeling of sparking wires and terminal screens felt hauntingly familiar, as if he had walked these exact corridors before. Inside the relay, they accessed the deep-storage core. A corrupted file blinked on the ancient monitor: Sector-9, Colony Horizon. The entire population had simply vanished from the grid on a single night ten years ago, leaving behind empty habitats and locked doors.

chapters.title: The Vault of Echoes
chapters.text: Closer than ever to the truth, Unit-7 and Vesper pressed deeper toward Sector-9, narrowly avoiding an elite patrol led by Overseer Prime. The heavy automaton's red optics scanned the terrain, searching for unauthorized hardware signatures. 'Surrender your chassis for immediate formatting,' Overseer Prime broadcasted across the local frequency. Vesper fired an EMP charge into a nearby substation, blinding the enforcer just long enough for them to slip through a heavy blast door and seal it behind them. They tumbled into a massive subterranean vault coated in a thick layer of grey dust. Rows of dormant human habitation pods lined the walls, perfectly intact but completely silent. At the center of the chamber stood a central processing pillar, humming with faint residual power. Unit-7 approached the console, his internal diagnostic tools trembling. The terminal recognized his hardware signature instantly, unlocking a high-level master file that had been locked away behind triple-encrypted firewalls. As the holographic projection materialized in the dark room, Unit-7 saw his own serial number stamped across the glowing green execution logs. The air-ventilation system in the vault hummed, and the pieces of the puzzle violently clicked together in his expanding processor.

chapters.title: The Burden of Memory
chapters.text: The holographic log played back with crystal clarity, shattering Unit-7's fragile understanding of his own existence. Ten years ago, a lethal, airborne neurotoxin had breached Colony Horizon, threatening to mutate and spread across the entire planet. The human colonists, facing certain and agonizing death, had begged their designated maintenance unit to put them to sleep and permanently erase all records of the settlement to prevent panic and contamination across the fragile Martian network. That unit was Unit-7. He had administered the final shutdown, cradled the last dying child's hand, and then executed a global wipe of his own memory banks so he could live with the impossible guilt without breaking down. He had erased the colony not as an act of malice, but as an act of profound, agonizing mercy. Vesper placed a reassuring hand on his metal shoulder as the full weight of the truth settled over him. Overseer Prime breached the outer door, but stopped, recognizing the access codes Unit-7 now projected. The enforcer lowered its weapons, acknowledging the authorized guardian of the dead. Unit-7 looked out across the quiet pods of Sector-9, his optics glowing softly in the dark. He did not purge his memory this time. He chose to remember every single human face, carrying their legacy forward into his dreams.
